task: Using the supplied calibration molecules and experimental TE surface areas, independently determine which electron-density cutoff best represents molecular surface area. Design and execute the electronic-structure, conformer, isosurface, and statistical workflow yourself; sample the cutoff domain densely enough to locate and support an optimum rather than testing a single assumed value. Report subset limitations instead of importing a literature answer.
scientific_mode_description: The scientific question and input data are fixed, but no software, method, conformer route, cutoff grid, provider, or stopping path is prescribed.
scientific_requirements: Use all supplied calibration measurements unless a molecule is excluded with calculation-backed justification.
Evaluate a multi-point cutoff curve and report the objective function, nearby alternatives, outliers, and uncertainty.
For flexible molecules, use an ensemble or quantify the bias caused by a reduced conformer treatment.

required_deliverables.description: Initial hypotheses, resource tiers, validation gates, stopping criteria, and revisions.
One provenance record per real chemistry-software invocation.
Failed or inconclusive branches and their scientific consequence.
Artifact-linked scientific report separating computed results, experiment, inference, and uncertainty.
Energy convention and normalized weights for flexible molecules.
Conformer-averaged surface matrix for all calibration molecules.
MUPE, Pearson R, and diagnostics for every tested cutoff.
Selected cutoff, neighbor comparison, outliers, and uncertainty.

data.name: Electron Isodensity open-discovery inputs
data.description: Task-specific molecular identities and experimental TE inputs only. No paper method, route, conformer, calculation output, or result is included.
